title: compatibility-validation: multiplexed stream/function-handshake for newly onboarded model variants
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Verify that newly onboarded model variants (including quantized and sharded builds) correctly support multiplexed streaming output and external function/tool invocation with version-pinning semantics, and produce stable, publishable performance profiles. Scope includes: handshake semantics, chunk affinity, backpressure handling, function-call framing and result fidelity, and interplay with version pinning + automatic fallback. Deliverables: compatibility matrix, automated conformance tests, published perf profiles for model-catalog, rollout checklist, and follow-up bug fixes.
acceptance_criteria: All target model variants pass the streaming handshake conformance suite (handshake/ack semantics, stream-id preservation) across supported runtimes and quantization modes
Function/tool call invocations maintain argument fidelity and deterministic mapping to tool responses across chunk boundaries (>=99.5% fidelity on synthetic suite)
Backpressure and client disconnects do not leak KV cache entries or orphan calls (zero memory growth in 1M-request soak test)
Published perf profiles (p50/p95 token latency, max throughput, memory footprint) for each model variant are uploaded to the model-catalog with reproducible harness config
Version pinning tests validate that pinned clients remain on chosen variant during canary/rollout and automatically fallback to compatible variant if pinned variant is evicted or unhealthy
test_plan: Build conformance harness: client-side emulator that can run multiplexed streams, inject out-of-order chunks, simulate tool proxies, and assert call/response lineage
Run synthetic workloads: low-latency and high-throughput profiles, with mix of long generations and short tool calls; measure P50/P95 latency, throughput, and error rates
Soak tests: 72-hour soak with sustained concurrency to evaluate memory growth and KV cache leak vectors
Chaos tests: kill worker processes, simulate network partition, and assert pinned-client behavior and graceful fallback
Cross-runner test: validate on CUDA and CPU-only quantized runner configurations where applicable
progress_updates: 2025-03-02: Kickoff meeting with runtime and onboarding teams. Agreed to include quantized fp16 and int8 builds in scope. Action: runtime to provide worker debug hooks by 2025-03-06 (assigned to Ravi).
2025-03-04: Initial conformance harness skeleton submitted. Client emulator supports multiplexed stream IDs and basic chunk reassembly. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4862
2025-03-05: Discovered a race in handshake ACK handling with shard-aware runtime; created short-term mitigation to retry on timeout. Created bug ENG-76100 to track permanent fix.

2025-03-07: Ran first throughput sweep against rw-instruct-4x-quantized on staging; observed increased function-call latency under high concurrency due to serialization in tool marshaller. Proposed change: move marshaller to streaming path and add per-call buffers. Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Streaming+Tool+Marshaller+Design

2025-03-08: Security review kickoff scheduled for 2025-03-10 to validate tool invocation isolation and KMS access patterns for private deploys. Noted requirement to audit tool call logs for PII leakage before publishing perf profiles.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Function-call marshalling adds CPU serialization hotspot under high concurrency. Mitigation: implement streaming marshaller with per-connection buffers and backpressure-aware batching.

Risk: Pinned clients could observe inconsistent behavior during canary rollouts. Mitigation: add explicit routing header honoring pin and a canary-health probe that disables rollouts for pinned namespaces.
Risk: Publishing perf profiles that leak internal env details or PII. Mitigation: sanitize logs, run privacy filter, and require security sign-off before model-catalog publication.
next_steps: Complete full conformance suite run against three model variants (baseline, quantized-int8, sharded) by 2025-03-12
Address marshaller refactor and land PR for streaming marshaller by 2025-03-14
Coordinate with Console team to add a per-model streaming/function-call health dashboard for rollout visibility
Complete security review and obtain sign-off prior to publishing perf profiles
